gw_awgengine.backup.readme:
Kaskad: a backup before the AmneziaWG engine change ({reason}), {at}.
To restore by hand: put the files back (state.json and secrets.json into /etc/kaskad, awg*/ into /etc/kaskad/gw), then run kaskadctl gw apply.
gw_awgengine.benefit.cpu: Plain VPN: half the CPU for the same traffic (100 Mbit/s — ≈25 % vs ≈50 %), a 10–20 % higher ceiling.
gw_awgengine.benefit.memory: Memory: amneziawg-go takes 0.9–1.4 GB under load (on 2 GB servers it ran out of memory); the module needs no memory of its own.
gw_awgengine.benefit.transit: Transit (protocol → leg to an exit): 2–3 times more traffic on the same CPU.
gw_awgengine.block.disk: Low disk space: {free} MB free, but the compiler, kernel headers and the build need about {need} MB.
gw_awgengine.block.headers: There are no headers for the running kernel {kernel} (package linux-headers-{kernel}) — the module can’t be built. Updating the system and restarting usually helps (apt update && apt full-upgrade, then reboot); a hosting provider’s kernel may have no headers at all.
gw_awgengine.block.host: A kernel module can’t be loaded here: {why}.
gw_awgengine.block.kernel_old: Linux kernel {kernel} is too old for the module ({min} or newer is needed).
gw_awgengine.block.no_apt: No apt: the compiler and kernel headers can’t be installed (the module builds on Debian and Ubuntu).
gw_awgengine.block.no_dkms: The dkms package isn’t in the repositories — check apt update and the package sources.
gw_awgengine.check.can: The kernel module can be turned on here.
gw_awgengine.check.cannot: The kernel module can’t be turned on here:
gw_awgengine.check.facts: kernel {kernel}, CPUs {cpus}, RAM {mem}, free disk space {free}
gw_awgengine.check.mix: The kernel module can be built here, but mixing gets in the way:
gw_awgengine.err.cannot: The kernel module can’t be turned on here: {why} Everything stays on userspace amneziawg-go.
gw_awgengine.err.mix: amneziawg-go and the kernel module can’t be mixed: {mix} To turn the module on anyway (mixed mode): kaskadctl gw awg engine kernel --force.
gw_awgengine.err.target: The AmneziaWG engine is kernel (kernel module) or program (userspace, amneziawg-go).
gw_awgengine.fallback.not_loaded: the module isn’t loaded for this kernel
gw_awgengine.host.no_modules: no /proc/modules — kernel modules can’t be loaded here (a container)
gw_awgengine.import.dir: {what} is a folder, but a Kaskad AmneziaWG export file is needed.
gw_awgengine.import.foreign_inbounds: {what} has protocols that aren’t AmneziaWG ({kinds}) — not importing.
gw_awgengine.import.foreign_secrets: {what} has secrets that aren’t AmneziaWG ones ({n}) — not importing.
gw_awgengine.import.net: the gateway network is {file} in the file and {here} here — device addresses are taken from the file
gw_awgengine.import.not_export: {what} isn’t a Kaskad AmneziaWG export file (it’s made by “Export” in menu 17 → Protocols → AmneziaWG engine or in the panel).
gw_awgengine.import.not_json: {what} isn’t a Kaskad AmneziaWG export file: it isn’t JSON inside (another file, or it was cut off while copying).
gw_awgengine.import.partial: {what} is incomplete: no “{part}” section — export again.
gw_awgengine.import.unreadable: {what} can’t be read (no permission, or it isn’t a regular file).
gw_awgengine.import.version: {what} is an export of another Kaskad version: update Kaskad on this server and try again.
gw_awgengine.log.import: GW AWG import: {path} — inbounds {inbounds}, users +{users}, devices +{devices}
gw_awgengine.mix.inbound: Protocol {title}: the kernel module of this server lacks the set of fixes for this line (it didn’t build here or the module hasn’t been rebuilt yet), and {cost}. What to do: rebuild the module — kaskadctl gw accel on (menu 17 → Protocols → AmneziaWG engine → 1); if it doesn’t take, move the devices to AmneziaWG 2.0 and remove protocol {line}, or keep the whole server on userspace.
gw_awgengine.mix.key_unknown: an AmneziaWG key of an unknown line
gw_awgengine.mix.leg: Exit “{name}” — {what}: {why}, and {cost}. What to do: replace this exit with an AmneziaWG 2.0 key — or keep the whole server on userspace.
gw_awgengine.mix.leg31: the kernel module of this server lacks Kaskad’s set of fixes, and without it the module as an AmneziaWG 3.1 client doesn’t connect to a server on amneziawg-go (issue #222); rebuild the module — kaskadctl gw accel on (menu 17 → Protocols → AmneziaWG engine → 1)
gw_awgengine.mix.leg_other: the kernel module doesn’t run such a leg
gw_awgengine.mix.leg_set: the kernel module of this server lacks Kaskad’s set of fixes, and legs of this line were tested on the module only with it; rebuild the module — kaskadctl gw accel on (menu 17 → Protocols → AmneziaWG engine → 1)
gw_awgengine.mix.warning: mixed mode: {lines} of AmneziaWG on userspace while the AmneziaWG engine is the kernel module — speed in one direction drops 2.5–3 times (kaskadctl gw awg engine — what to do)
gw_awgengine.mix_cost: amneziawg-go and the kernel module can’t be mixed — transit to clients gets slower
gw_awgengine.pays.memory: Memory is {mem}, and amneziawg-go already takes {rss} MB — on 2 GB servers it ran out of memory.
gw_awgengine.pays.transit: The server runs transit (AmneziaWG protocol → AmneziaWG leg to an exit): here the module carries 2–3 times more traffic.
gw_awgengine.plan.install: Will be installed: a compiler and kernel headers ({pkgs}, ≈{mb} MB); the module builds in 1–3 min, then a self-test. {reconnect}
gw_awgengine.plan.ready: The compiler and kernel headers are already installed: build and self-test take 1–2 min. {reconnect}
gw_awgengine.reason.line: there is line {line} — the kernel module doesn’t run it, the whole server is on userspace
gw_awgengine.reason.mix: there is a line the kernel module doesn’t run ({what}) — the whole server is on userspace
gw_awgengine.reason.rollback: after the switch to {target} none of the {alive} live clients reconnected within {minutes} min — restored {was}
gw_awgengine.reconnect: AmneziaWG clients reconnect on their own, usually within 15–25 seconds; WireGuard isn’t affected.
gw_awgengine.risk.build: Needs a compiler and kernel headers (≈200 MB); on a kernel update the module rebuilds itself, and if it doesn’t build, AmneziaWG goes back to userspace on its own.
gw_awgengine.risk.panic: A bug in the module brings down the whole server kernel, not one process (a panic on wrong parameters is known — issue #254; Kaskad doesn’t let such parameters into the module).
gw_awgengine.say.rollback: Clients didn’t come back within {minutes} min — restoring the previous AmneziaWG engine…
gw_awgengine.say.wait: Waiting for AmneziaWG clients to reconnect ({alive} were live, up to {minutes} min)…
gw_awgengine.short.inbound: protocol {line} without the module’s set of fixes
gw_awgengine.short.leg_set: leg {line} without the module’s set of fixes
gw_awgengine.text.default: AmneziaWG engine: kernel module (the default for new protocols)
gw_awgengine.text.kernel_forced: AmneziaWG engine: kernel module (mixing turned on manually)
gw_awgengine.text.never: AmneziaWG engine: userspace — the kernel module hasn’t been turned on yet (recommended)
gw_awgengine.text.new_kernel: AmneziaWG engine: userspace — the server now runs kernel {now} (was {was}): the kernel module can be turned on again (recommended)
gw_awgengine.warn.kernel_untested: Kernel {kernel} wasn’t tested in the lab: if the module doesn’t build for it, everything stays on userspace (automatic rollback).
gw_awgengine.warn.no_way_back: the previous AmneziaWG engine didn’t come back: {why}
gw_awgengine.warn.rebuild: The kernel module in memory lacks the set of fixes (3.1 protocol, 3.1 and 1.x legs): the switch rebuilds it (1–3 min) and reloads it — {reconnect}
gw_awgengine.warn.set_failed_before: Last time the module’s set of fixes for line 3.1 didn’t take here ({why}) — the switch will try again; if it doesn’t take, the 3.1 protocol and the 3.1 and 1.x legs stay on userspace, and that is mixing.
